svg.font-family: Inter, Segoe UI, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif
svg.title: Figure 2. Three observers of one page load
svg.desc: One page load is watched by three separate observers. The network path sees the destination address, the domain name lookup, and the hostname in the connection handshake. The server sees the request headers, the cookies, and the origin you came from. Script running on the page measures the device itself: canvas rendering, graphics strings, fonts, audio, screen geometry, time zone and core count. A note explains which of these transport encryption protects and which it does not.
svg.text: Figure 2: One Page Load, Three Observers
Each observer sees a different set of things. A control that helps against one of them can do nothing about the other two.
your provider, the network you are on, anyone in between

g.text: Your address, and therefore your approximate location
The domain name lookup, unless the lookup itself is encrypted
The hostname in the connection handshake, unless the handshake is encrypted
The size and timing of every exchange
Characteristics of your operating system network stack

svg.text: OBSERVER 2: THE SERVER, AND EVERY THIRD PARTY IT LOADS

g.text: Your address again, plus the exact time
Your request headers: browser and version, languages you accept
Any cookie that this domain set before
Which site you arrived from, at domain level
Tracking parameters carried in the address itself
Which resources your browser already had cached

svg.text: OBSERVER 3: SCRIPT RUNNING ON THE PAGE
this is the one that measures your device

g.text: An audio signal, processed and hashed
Screen geometry, colour depth, pixel ratio
Processor core count and memory hints

svg.text: Transport encryption protects the content of observer 2, and nothing in observer 1 or observer 3. Encryption is not a privacy control here.
Module 1, Lesson 1, Myth 3 said this in the abstract. This figure is the same statement with the field names filled in.
